module.purpose: Groups coincident comment pins in page space and provides stable membership comparisons and liveness checks for the canvas overlay.
module.summary: This module converts comment-thread anchors into quantized page-space stack keys, groups same-page threads into ordered multi-member stacks, compares stack maps by membership, and verifies whether an open stack remains represented on the canvas. It deliberately keys by page coordinates rather than camera-dependent screen positions, preserving overlay state when members change while allowing reactive liveness checks to observe anchor movement.
module.businessContext: Supports collaborative canvas commenting by consolidating overlapping comment pins into count badges and maintaining their open-stack state. Failures can hide comments, create unstable badges, or leave stale stack selections visible.
functions: pinStackKey (~L14-16): Quantizes a page point into its stable stack identity
computePinStacks (~L28-59): Groups same-page anchored threads into ordered stack memberships
pinStacksEqual (~L69-85): Compares stack maps for identical membership and ordering
isOpenStackKeyLive (~L94-108): Checks whether an open stack remains present and positioned

import type { Editor, TLCommentThread } from 'tldraw'
import { anchorPagePoint } from './thread-state'

detail.name: pinStackKey
preconditions: The point provides x and y coordinate values usable in numeric division and rounding.
postconditions: Returns a string containing the rounded x coordinate divided by PIN_STACK_QUANTUM, followed by a colon and the rounded y coordinate divided by PIN_STACK_QUANTUM.
invariants: The key uses the same PIN_STACK_QUANTUM for both coordinates.
The x and y components are separated by exactly one colon.
edgeCases: Coordinates on or near quantization boundaries are rounded using JavaScript Math.round semantics.
Negative, fractional, or zero coordinates are processed through the same division-and-rounding operation.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns the text form <rounded x / PIN_STACK_QUANTUM>:<rounded y / PIN_STACK_QUANTUM>.
detail.summary: Converts a point into a deterministic pin-stack key by quantizing and rounding its coordinates.

specLiterals.role: Separates the quantized x and y coordinate components in the returned stack key.

units.name: computePinStacks

detail.name: computePinStacks
detail.signature: function computePinStacks(editor: Editor, threads: readonly TLCommentThread[]): Map<string, readonly string[]>
preconditions: editor provides the current page ID and supports resolving thread anchors to page points.
threads contains TLCommentThread values with pageId, anchor, id, and createdAt fields.
postconditions: Returns a Map whose keys are thread IDs belonging to stacks of at least two eligible threads.
Each returned value contains the IDs of all threads in that stack, ordered by ascending createdAt and then lexicographically by ID.
Threads from pages other than the editor's current page and threads whose anchors cannot be resolved are absent from the result.
The input threads collection is not reordered or otherwise mutated.
invariants: Threads are grouped only when they belong to the current page and resolve to the same pin-stack key.
Every ID in a returned stack maps to the same readonly ID array for that stack.
A group with fewer than two eligible threads produces no entries.
edgeCases: An empty thread collection returns an empty Map.
Threads from a different page are ignored.
Threads with anchors that do not resolve to a page point are ignored.
A single eligible thread at a point is not returned as a stack.
Threads with equal createdAt values are ordered lexicographically by ID.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns a Map<string, readonly string[]> keyed by each thread ID in a multi-thread stack. Each value is the ordered list of all thread IDs sharing that stack.
detail.summary: Computes stacks of comment-thread IDs for visible threads anchored at the same page point on the editor's current page. Only groups containing at least two eligible threads are returned, with each member mapped to the deterministically ordered IDs of its stack.

specTests.then: The result contains both thread IDs as keys, and both keys map to the same ID list ordered by ascending createdAt.
Both IDs map to the ordered list ["a", "b"].

units.name: pinStacksEqual

detail.name: pinStacksEqual
detail.signature: function pinStacksEqual(a: Map<string, string[]>, b: Map<string, string[]>): boolean
preconditions: Both arguments are map-like collections whose values are ordered groups.
postconditions: Returns true only when both maps have the same size, every key in the second map exists in the first map, and corresponding groups are equal by ordered element value.
Returns false when the map sizes differ, a key is absent from the first map, a group length differs, or any corresponding element differs.
invariants: Input maps and groups are not mutated.
Reference-identical maps return true without inspecting their contents.
edgeCases: The same map reference returns true.
Maps with different sizes return false.
A key present in the second map but absent from the first returns false.
Groups with different lengths return false.
Groups with the same elements in a different order return false.
Distinct group arrays with equal ordered elements return true.
detail.summary: Determines whether two pin-stack maps contain the same keys and equivalent ordered groups. It treats identical map references as equal and otherwise compares each group's length and element order.

specTests.when: pinStacksEqual is called with those maps.

units.name: isOpenStackKeyLive

detail.name: isOpenStackKeyLive
preconditions: stacks is iterable and exposes thread identifiers through keys().
threadsById provides thread lookup by identifier.
Each resolved thread has an anchor usable by anchorPagePoint.
postconditions: Returns true if at least one resolved thread has a page point whose pinStackKey equals key.
Returns false when no resolved thread has a matching live point.
invariants: Only thread identifiers present in stacks are considered.
Threads whose anchor does not resolve to a page point are ignored.
Evaluation stops once a matching live stack key is found.
edgeCases: A stack identifier with no corresponding entry in threadsById is skipped.
A resolved thread whose anchor produces no page point does not make the key live.
An empty stacks collection returns false.
If multiple threads are present, the result is true when any one resolves to key and false when none do.
detail.summary: Determines whether any thread represented by the provided stacks currently resolves to the specified pin stack key.

specTests.when: isOpenStackKeyLive is called with that key

specTests.then: It returns true without requiring every stack entry to match.
